_comment: CLUSTER 3 -- THE GO-OFF IS SIZED IN GENERIC MANA WHILE THE FINISHER IS PAID IN {C} PIPS.
Rule DEPLOYED fires (loop + Essence Depleter on the battlefield + three {C} sources + a draw
source) and the plan promises `blink Cloud of Faeries x14`. The apply runs all fourteen and
drains exactly NINE times: opponent 20 -> 11, and stops.
THE ARITHMETIC. The recognizer's own trace says the loop is healthy:
[edf-goff] t5 ... net=3 refund=6 cost=3 drain=1/2 kmax=3 afford=3 n=14
14 iterations x net 3 = 42 generic mana against the Depleter's 20 drains x {1}{C} = 40. On
GENERIC mana the sizing is right. On COLOURLESS it is not: Cloud of Faeries untaps TWO lands,
the yield order takes Kitchen (5) and the {C}-starved reservation forces the other slot onto a
{C} land (1), and Eldrazi Displacer's {2}{C} eats that one {C} every single pass. So the loop's
colourless net per iteration is ZERO, while the drain needs one {C} per activation -- the only
{C} the Depleter ever sees is the initial untapped supply. Nine drains, then nothing.
WHAT THE RULE TABLE CHECKS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. comborules::ColorlessSourceCount counts {C}
SOURCES ON THE BOARD (three here, so C1 and C2 both hold) and MTG_COMBO_OFF_BANKABLE prices the
path in generic mana. Neither consults the recognizer's loop.net_c -- the per-iteration
colourless NET -- even though FlickerLoop already computes it and it is the quantity that
actually gates a {C}-pip finisher. A board can hold five colourless sources and still feed the
sink at net zero.
SWAP THE OUTLET AND IT WINS. Emiel the Blessed's blink cost is {3} with no {C} pip, so the same
untap leaves its {C} free: the sibling synthetic state A_emiel_cloud_fin-bf-depleter is class
(a), offered and winning. This is the same Displacer-vs-Emiel divide the committed fixtures
edf_co_4 (single {C}, ABSENT) and edf_co_5 (two {C} + Drake, OFFERED) already pin at the
display end; it simply is not pinned at the EXECUTION end.
WHICH CLASS THIS IS is a question for the user, and that is why it is catalogued rather than
fixed: either the go-off count must be sized by the {C} pip supply as well as the mana (the
MTG_EDF_GOFF_C_ITERS axis, which does not bind on this path), or the rules must require
loop.net_c > 0 for any {C}-pip finisher -- and the second narrows the display, which is the
user's call under the aggressive-display doctrine.
EXPECTED TO FAIL until that ruling lands.
